newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: CAM, Sime Darby in vegetable venture.
newsitem.headline: CAM, Sime Darby in vegetable venture.

text.p: CAM International Holdings Ltd said on Monday it was partnering Malaysian conglomerate Sime Darby Bhd in an aeroponic vegetable venture in Singapore.

Sime Darby's subsidiary Consolidated Plantations Bhd, would acquire 5.88 million shares or a 49 percent stake of the enlarged capital of Aero-Green Technology (S) Pte Ltd for Singapore $10.88 million, a statement from CAM said.
The aeroponic method enables vegetables to grow without soil, with their roots suspended in the air. Nutrients are supplied through fine mists from a spray system.
The Malaysian farms are expected to be between six and 10 hectares in size. The first would be located near Kuala Lumpur.
Aero-Green currently operates an aeroponic farm in Singapore that produces lettuces and other temperate and sub-tropical vegetables.
Work on a second Singapore farm is scheduled to start in August and should be completed by March 1998.

Aero-Green, set up in 1996 by CAM and other minor shareholders to undertake large-scale commercial production of aeroponic vegetables in Singapore, would see its paid-up capital rise to S$12 million on completion of the deal, it said.
The remaining 51 percent of Aero-Green would be owned by CAM's unit CAM Agro-Innovation (S) Pte Ltd (CAI) and other founding members of Aero-Green.
CAM and Sime Darby, through their units, would set up a 30:70 joint venture company in Malaysia to establish and operate aeroponic farms there, the statement said.
